title: I'm building a voxel robot action game with a studio of AI agents.
author: Kenjirio
selftext:
This is EXO: Hold the Line, a voxel robot action game where you pilot one war frame against waves of hundreds of machines. It's still very early alpha, with lots of bugs and unfinished work, but I'm proud of how far it's come. The video is about 9 minutes running through a few builds of the first class, Vanguard.

Quick facts:

* Three.js and plain JavaScript, runs in the browser
* No 3D models. Every robot, prop and arena is built in code from concept images
* I'm not a dev (and I hope this encourages other non-devs to start building too)

How it started

Not long ago I stumbled on an open-source [voxel action game](https://github.com/wuxie888/voxel-three-kingdoms) on GitHub (MIT licensed, by BubuAi). I'd wanted to build a game of my own for a while, but with the ambition I had I assumed I'd need an engine like Unity just to start. Then I saw how well this demo played, so I used it as the base and built from there.

The best part is that because everything is code, building it with AI is extremely efficient. I've made a lot of progress considering how early this is.

**How it's made**

I run it like a small studio inside Hermes Agent. An orchestrator agent (Claude Opus) plans the work and hands tasks to role agents: engineer, animator, VFX, level designer, game designer and concept artist. Every task runs in its own git worktree, and a merge queue runs the checks and lands the finished work. Cheaper models (DeepSeek, Sonnet) do the bulk of the work, and GPT does the concept art.

My biggest unlock was Hermes Agent itself. I slowly moved my setup over from Claude Code across a few weeks, and the moment I knew the workflows were working was when DeepSeek V4.1 Flash built a better map than Opus 5.5. After that, the kanban boards made everything fast.

Now I just chat with Opus, and he turns my brain dumps of ideas and bug fixes into tasks for an army of agents, usually 10 to 20 running at once while I'm active, split between DS, sonnet and occasionally Opus. I get the next build, playtest it, rant about what to improve, and go again. That's the main loop.

**The hard part**

Getting the workflows to my liking. I'm a visual guy, and it took a while to get the skills for characters, props, and especially combat skills and VFX to a place I'm happy with. There are still plenty of tweaks to make everywhere to make things smoother.

Right now my focus is getting the combat system and all 7 classes fully working, each with at least 3 test builds. The bigger idea is that you build your own combos, and a loot system makes every fight worth it.

If you want to follow along, there's a mailing list here: [https://exo-hold-the-line.vercel.app](https://exo-hold-the-line.vercel.app/) I'll try to get a playable build up soon to get feedback!

Happy to answer anything about the agent setup. It's still a work in progress.

replies.body: Cloud atm, mainly through Opencode go and the direct api

comments.author: Muanh
comments.body: Are the agents running on a single computer? How do they test?

replies.author: Kenjirio
replies.body:
Yeah, MacBook Pro 24Gb so it is a great help. The testing is the best part because everything is just code they can use scripts and browser use to test anything they need. I first had the agent study the base repo to understand how skills etc were made and then reversed engineered the process into skills and testing gates so visuals would look good. The difference is night and day when the agent uses the skills vs ignores them. 

Right now the testing is the heaviest and slowest part of the resources but I’m working on optimising that.

replies.author: Muanh
replies.body: So you have multiple agents run the full game on the same machine? Have you thought about a testing que where one agent is allowed to test the full game?

replies.author: Kenjirio
replies.body: i've been thinking about making a lighter version of the game to specifically test parts that the agent needs. But your idea is interesting as well and i'll give it a try, do you currently do that in your workflow and if so how has it been?

replies.author: Muanh
replies.body: No, I’m not running an agent right now. Currently using T3, but your post sounded interesting. So was thinking on how that would work for my project.

replies.author: Muanh
replies.body: One other question. Are you running Hermes on Anthropic subscription or what are you using there?

replies.author: Kenjirio
replies.body: Yea on the sub, opus 5.5 high for the main coordinator agent and sonnet 5.5 medium or high for workers in addition to deepseek. Occasionally an opus high worker for harder stuff.

replies.author: Muanh
replies.body: Isn't that against anthropic TOS? How are you connecting the sub to Hermes?

replies.author: Kenjirio
replies.body: Hermes shipped an update which is compliant or something like that. Saw it on X. All I know is that it works now lol.

replies.author: Muanh
replies.body: Do you have the link? Very interested to start setting this up myself.

replies.author: Kenjirio
replies.body: Just download the Hermes agent app from nous research and the setup will guide you

replies.author: Kenjirio
replies.body: And a cheap codex sub for img gen for ideation and guiding visuals for characters etc.

comments.author: Kenjirio
comments.body:
Ahh so as I said before I was using CC this whole time for other work as well. But it required me working on too many moving parts to handle so that’s why I switched to Hermes (and they recently added full anthropic sub support).

Kanban board feature is OP for organising work and just have your main agent create a dashboard and tweak it to your liking so you can see what’s up. Sub profiles for the different aspects and ways to force them to use the skills and workflows you set.

If you need any help send me a dm and I can have my agent give you a summary of the setup so yours can have a starting point. Once you have skills locked in and a strong workflow one chat can handle all the dispatching etc.
